findings.asked: Mean and SD, then the effect of adding 3 to every value.
findings.wentWrong: The fx column was squared instead of f x squared; adding 3 was applied to the SD as well as the mean.
findings.rule: Adding a constant moves the mean and leaves the SD unchanged; multiplying scales both.

findings.asked: SD of five marks, then scaling with y = mx + n.
findings.wentWrong: About a third got only the mean mark; just over half handled the scaling - strange equations in m and n appeared.
findings.rule: New mean = m x old mean + n; new SD = m x old SD.

ruleToRemember: For y = mx + n: mean of y = m(mean of x) + n and SD of y = m(SD of x) - the added constant never touches the spread.
